prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This 2024 manifesto sets out a “contract” of policies across immigration, public spending, the economy, public services, energy, security, and governance, alongside estimated costings and savings.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration and stop small-boat crossings via detention, deportation, and returns to France.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 to “make work pay.”
- Cut energy bills by scrapping Net Zero policies and expanding domestic oil and gas.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential migration; create a new Department of Immigration; leave the European Convention on Human Rights; bar asylum from safe countries; offshore processing; no legal aid for non‑citizens; immediate deportation of foreign offenders; restrict student dependents.
- Require five years’ residency and employment for benefits.
- Introduce a 20% employer National Insurance rate for foreign workers (exemptions for essential health/care and very small firms).

Public spending and regulation
- End Bank of England interest on QE reserves; require 5% efficiency savings across departments; halve overseas aid; strengthen HMRC tax collection; repeal retained EU laws and other regulations viewed as burdensome.

Personal taxation and cost of living
- Lift income tax start point to £20,000; move higher rate to £70,000.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p, scrap VAT on energy and environmental levies.
- Reform Stamp Duty (0% below £750k; 2% to £1.5m; 4% above).
- Restore VAT refunds for tourists; raise the IHT threshold to £2m and set 20% above that (charity alternative).

Business and jobs
- Raise the corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut the main rate to 20%, then 15% in year 3.
- Abolish IR35; raise the VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.
- Planning reform, deregulation (including easier hiring/firing), and tax simplification.

NHS
- Zero basic rate income tax for frontline NHS and social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; write off fees over service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance; patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks.
- Efficiency and management reforms; “Pharmacy First” approach; inquiry into excess deaths and vaccine harms.

Energy and Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero and related subsidies; expand North Sea and shale; accelerate SMRs; support other technologies.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers; zero‑tolerance approach; expand stop and search; mandatory sentences for violent/drug offences; remove DE&I roles.
- Increase criminal justice budget; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 detention places; measures on grooming gangs and youth crime.

Education and families
- Curriculum changes; ban gender transitioning/social transitioning in schools; single‑sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap interest on student loans; stricter university entry; more exclusions with expanded PRUs; 2‑year degrees.
- Marriage tax allowance (as finances allow); front‑load Child Benefit ages 1–4; smartphone and social media measures.

Housing and transport
- Fast‑track brownfield development; local priority in social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility for landlords; drop the Renters’ Reform Bill; strengthen leaseholder protections.
- Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs; keep ICE cars; accelerate regional transport; new utility ownership model (50% public, 50% UK pension funds), cap standing charges.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Raise farming budget to £3bn; remove climate‑related farm subsidies; support country sports; competition and “Buy British” measures; cut red tape.
- Tighten control of UK waters; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild domestic processing and fleet; sustainability regime.

Pensions and social care
- Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax practices in large care providers; pension system review; implement Mineworkers’ Pension recommendations.

Constitution and governance
- Leave the ECHR; reform the House of Lords and civil service leadership; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Sovereignty and free‑speech measures; reform the BBC and scrap the licence fee; new national holidays; anti‑corruption unit.

Funding (manifesto estimates)
- Potential savings: ~£150bn/year plus £10bn/year from assumed growth.
- Annual costs of measures: ~£141bn/year.
